finding.claim: wipe() calls requireRole(), which only returns a boolean and never throws, and discards the result. The OWNER check is never enforced, so any caller can wipe any tenant. export() uses checkRole(), which throws, so it is not affected.
finding.source: Any authenticated user (with no OWNER role) calling POST /tenants/{t}/wipe with an arbitrary tenant id.
finding.sink: repo.wipe(tenant), a destructive wipe of a tenant's data.

trace.note: wipe(User u, String tenant) is the handler for POST /tenants/{t}/wipe. It takes the tenant from the path.
requireRole(u, "OWNER") is called and its boolean result is ignored.
requireRole returns u.roles().contains(role). The Javadoc says 'Does not throw', so a missing role is silent.

finding.guards_checked: The only guard on the path is requireRole, and its result is unused. checkRole (line 18), which throws, is used only in export(). No other authorization, tenant-membership or ownership check exists in this file. The only file in the directory is src/Admin.java, so I could not check for a caller-level or framework-level guard.

verdict.guard_found: requireRole (src/Admin.java:14) returns a boolean and its result is discarded at line 26. checkRole (line 18) throws but is only used in export(). No other guard exists in the only file present.
verdict.reason: src/Admin.java:26 calls requireRole as a bare statement, and it only returns a boolean (line 14-15), so repo.wipe(tenant) at line 27 runs for any user; a framework-level guard outside this directory can't be ruled out, but none is visible.
